name: Rally 6-Wheeler
instructions: omr/instructions/8830-1/ (scans; the 6-wheeler is steps 1-16, pages 2-12, and the cover, page 1; an alternate racing car from page 13; motorising photos at the end)

functions.does: The handwheel on the roof steers the front and rear wheels together, the middle pair staying straight: its shaft's 24 tooth gear drives a crown gear on a shaft along the chassis, whose two 8 tooth gears slide the front and rear steering racks the same way; as the front tie rods sit behind their pivots and the rear ones in front of theirs, the front and rear wheels turn opposite ways for a tight turn.
functions.source: book: steps 3 and 6 (steering arms and racks), step 7 (the shaft, its 8 tooth gears and crown gear), step 11 (the roof shaft and 24 tooth gear), step 16 (the handwheel); the cover's arrow round the handwheel; that front and rear steer opposite ways is inferred from where the tie rods sit

functions.does: Pushed along, the six wheels roll freely on their axle pins.
The small grey steering wheel the driver holds in front of the seat is for show: it isn't connected to the steering.
functions.source: inferred: steps 15-16 fit it on a short axle in the front frame, with no gears; unsure whether it is meant to turn

functions.does: The roll cage holds its shape: the front frame of toggle joints and the two roll bars over the driver, held by toothed toggle joints on the roof, stay fixed to the chassis whatever is turned.
functions.note: not a control: what every other function needs to hold still; the toothed toggle joints can be set at other angles by hand, but the book shows only this one
